subject: Finscape: deterministic warm-pool + telemetry export commitment
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, Alex Quinn <alex.quinn@finscape.com>
Cc: procurement@finscape.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finscape: deterministic warm-pool + telemetry export commitment

Alex / team —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick summary and the ask so Product & Eng can adjudicate: Finscape is contracting for enterprise usage (DEAL-3829) and requires two specific commitments for go-live acceptance:

1) Deterministic warm-pool guarantee: an SLA-style objective that a pinned warm pool (model residency) will be available for their production traffic window (Mon–Fri PST 08:00–18:00) with p99 latency target of 120ms for short-chat flows. This is a billing-impacting residency hold — they expect a small monthly premium for reservation but need hard guarantees for performance.

2) Telemetry export: continuous delivery of a structured telemetry stream (redacted tokens) to their SIEM/S3 bucket. They want a vendor-side export with a predefined field map (attached CSV) and a one-week retention of raw traces on our side for troubleshooting.

I realize both items touch product policy and capacity planning. Can we get a short assessment on feasibility, rough engineering cost (person-weeks), and any blockers we should surface to procurement/legal?

I attached a draft SOW that procurement asked for (Finscape_SOW_v1.pdf) and the telemetry field map they expect.

Proposed next step: internal alignment call with Eng/Product today or tomorrow then a 30-min customer follow-up by Thursday.

Thanks —
Tessa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Finscape: deterministic warm-pool + telemetry export commitment

Tessa —

Quick technical clarifications from my side:

- Warm-pool: do we need a tenant-exclusive GPU pool (true isolation) or is a pinned residency with soft sharing acceptable if we guarantee primacy for scheduled windows? The engineering effort differs: exclusive pools imply infra capacity planning + reservation layer; pinned residency with priority routing is ~2–3w engineering + capacity cost modeling.

- Latency target: p99 120ms for "short-chat flows" — can you give a 95/99 token-length distribution sample (we can use your staging traces) so I can estimate kernel and batch sizing impact?

- Telemetry export: does Finscape need raw token-level traces or redacted/log-level events? The SOW mentions redacted tokens but their CSV maps include a few token-ish fields. Exporting raw traces requires additional PII review and might trigger security review. If it's log-level events (request_id, route, model, latency, sample_top_tokens) we can generally do it via existing export hooks.

I can spin up a quick perf estimate once I have the distribution and clarity on exclusivity.

—Dev
Lead Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Finscape: deterministic warm-pool + telemetry export commitment

Thanks for the clear ask, Tessa. High level assessment from Product:

Warm-pool options (tradeoffs):
- Option A: Dedicated tenant-exclusive pool (hard isolation) — PROS: simplest guarantee for customer, easier proof-of-SLA; CONS: high operational cost, longer lead time (capacity booking), requires Dedicated plan negotiation. Estimated eng + infra: 4–6 weeks to implement reservation gating + billing integration.

- Option B: Pinned residency with priority scheduling (soft exclusivity) — PROS: lower cost, faster (~2–3w), fits existing Dedicated/Dynamic routing pieces; CONS: possible tail cases during platform-wide spikes; mitigations: canary reservations and emergency overflow policies.

Telemetry export options:
- Level 1: Log-level events (request_id, route, model, latency, decision_flags) — we can deliver via existing export streams with small schema extension (~1w).
- Level 2: Pseudonymized token traces — needs security signoff; estimate 2–3w + compliance review.

Recommended path for DEAL-3829: propose Option B for warm-pool with a contractual fallback (priority + pre-warm hooks) and Level 1 telemetry delivery with a roadmap milestone to Level 2 after SOC review. This reduces go-live friction while giving Finscape a measurable commitment.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev to confirm capacity/latency estimate if we accept pinned residency + priority routing.
2) Tessa to confirm willingness for contractual fallback language (priority > absolute exclusivity).
3) Legal/procurement review of the SOW telemetry wording — cc'ing procurement thread is already present.

I can be available tomorrow 10–11am PT for a 30-min alignment if that helps finalize the customer ask.

—Marissa
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side to help you size: 

- We are fine with a pinned residency + priority routing (Option B) as long as the SOW includes a defined fallback and crediting behavior in the rare event we experience p99 breaches during our production window. We can accept a 30–60 minute RTO escalation path if needed.

- Telemetry: Level 1 (log-level events) is acceptable for go-live. We'll take weekly snapshots of relevant traces for deep-dive sessions but don't need token-level exports to start. The CSV includes some fields we plan to map client-side; feel free to ignore token columns until we complete the privacy signoff.

Timeline: we aim for a technical kickoff the week of July 5 and a production pilot by July 26. Procurement is ready to accept an amended SOW with the Option B/canary fallback language and a one-week trial period.

I'll attach the procurement template separately to procurement@finscape.com — they should be able to turn around redlines within 5 business days.

—Alex Quinn
Head of Integrations | Finscape Labs
